<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par112 />{{GHGheb|text=וָאֹֽמַר}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=38|verse=28}}, where the narrative breaks off in the middle of the sentence; 40:3 ({{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}, &c., wanting in the LXX); also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=13}} {{GHGheb|text=וְנָפַל הָאֹהֶל}} is altogether redundant; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=3|verse=13}} read, with Klostermann, the ''2nd sing. masc.'' instead of {{GHGheb|text=והגדתי}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=21|verse=12}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהֹשִׁ֫יבוּ}} is, no doubt, incorrectly repeated from verse 9, where it is an imperative.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|rr}}
Of other questionable instances, (α) the following, at any rate, may also be explained as frequentatives, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=23|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=38}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=38|verse=28|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=39|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=5|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=24|verse=11|hidebook=1}} (but even so {{GHGheb|text=וְאָֽמְרוּ}} would be expected); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=28|verse=26}} (parallel with an imperfect); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=5|verse=26}} (unless it is rather, ''yea, ye shall take up''; see above, ''x''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=26|verse=3}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=8|verse=36}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|ss}}
(β) A longer or constant continuance in a past state is perhaps represented by the perfect with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}} (as a variety of the frequentative perfect with {{GHGheb|text=וְ}}), in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=15|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=34|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=21|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=9|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=22|verse=3|hidebook=1}}b, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=3|verse=9}}. But the unusual ''perfects consec.'' in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=15|verse=3}}–11, 16:2–8 (ultimately parallel with an imperf. as in 17:9, 18:20), 18:12–21, 19:11–14.22.26–29.34, are without doubt rightly explained by Bennett ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|SBOT.|Sacred Books of the Old Testament, ed. by P. Haupt. Lpz. and Baltimore, 1893 ff.}}}}, Joshua, p. 23) as originally containing the directions either of God to Joshua or of Joshua to the people; cf. the evident trace of this in 15:4b. A redactor transformed the directions into a description but left the ''perfects consec.'', which are to be explained as in ''aa''. In the same way {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=29}} is most simply explained as repeated from 26:25.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|tt}}
(γ) The following are due to errors in the text, or to incorrect modes of expression: {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=36|verse=29}} f., {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=3|verse=23}},<ref>Or does {{GHGheb|text=ונעל}}, as a frequentative, imply fastening with several bolts? It is, at all events, to be noticed, that in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=18}} also {{GHGheb|text=ונעל}} follows an imperfect consecutive.</ref> 16:18 (read {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעֲלוּ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=38|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=19|verse=18|hidebook=1}} f. (read {{GHGheb|text=צָֽלְחוּ}} and {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעַבְרוּ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=3|verse=11}} (where {{GHGheb|text=ושאלת}} is, no doubt intentionally, assimilated to the four other perfects); 13:3, 20:21; {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=14|verse=7}} (where, with Stade, {{GHGheb|text=וְאֶת־הַסֶּ֫לַע תּפַשׁ}} should be read); 14:14, 18:4 (where, at any rate, {{GHGheb|text=וְשִׁבַּר}} might be taken as a frequentative, but not {{GHGheb|text=וכרת}}, &c.; evidently the perfects are co-ordinated only in form with {{GHGheb|text=הוּא הֵסִיר}}); 18:36, 21:15, 24:14, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=15}} (where {{GHGheb|text=וְהִכּוּ}}, but not {{GHGheb|text=וְנָֽתְנוּ}}, might be frequentative); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=7}} (omit {{GHGheb|text=וְיָֽצְאוּ}} with Stade, and read {{GHGheb|text=וְהַכּוּ}}); 20:22 ({{GHGheb|text=והשבתי}} {{GHGterm|Milʿêl}} before an imperfect consecutive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְאָכְלָה}} after an imperfect consecutive); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=12}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|112|uu}}
Finally, in {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=10|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=48|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=20|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=6|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=3|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=37|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=2}} {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}} is to be read throughout instead of {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיָה}}, but in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=38|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=וְהִיא}} with the LXX.<section end=par112 />

<section begin=par113 />{{center|{{Small-caps|B. The Infinitive and Participle.}}}}

<!-- section begins above -->{{GHGpar-heading|113|The Infinitive Absolute}}

Cf. the dissertation of J. Kahan, and, especially, the thorough investigation by E. Sellin, both entitled, ''Ueber die verbal-nominale Doppelnatur der hebräischen Participien und Infinitive'', &c., Lpz. 1889; F. Prätorius, ‘Ueber die sogen. Infin. absol. des Hebr.’ in {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1902, pp. 546 ff.

{{GHGmargin-letter|113|a}}
'''1.''' The infinitive absolute is employed according to § 45 to emphasize the idea of the verb ''in the abstract'', i.e. it speaks of an action (or state) without any regard to the agent or to the circumstances of time and mood under which it takes place. As the ''name'' of an action the infinitive absolute, like other nouns in the stricter sense,<section end=par113 /><noinclude>
